To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the prevalence of antibodies against the 128 kDa protein of H. pylori was higher in patients with gastric ulcer than in healthy subjects, and (ii) patients with gastric ulcer and antibodies against this protein had significantly higher levels than healthy subjects and patients with duodenal ulcer.

(i) the prevalence of antibodies against the CagA protein in patients with H. pylori infection is high (92%) in a population of patients with gastric cancer, but lower in patients with non-gastric cancer and in the healthy controls; (ii) the prevalence of IgA antibodies against CagA is significantly higher in patients with H.pylori infection, and in particular those with gastric cancer, than in the controls.

(1) a significant percentage of patients with chronic hepatitis C virus (HCV) infection are seropositive for anti-Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) antibodies and (2) the presence of antibodies against H. pylori is associated with the development of cirrhosis and the presence of HCV genotype 2b.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the molecular mechanisms of action of the anti-HIV-1 compounds.
the identification of the immunogenic proteins of and the development of a diagnostic test for this pathogen.
the development of a method for the detection of the presence of Helicobactrer pylori in gastric biopsy specimens.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the results are inconclusive and the test is not useful in the clinical setting.
there is no clear-cut answer to the question of the best method for serodiagnosis.
the results obtained with ELISA for detection of antibodies to H. pylori are not reliable and that they should not be used in clinical practice.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
this is the first study to evaluate the efficacy of a triple therapy regimen for HIV-infected patients who had failed fluconazole treatment of a fluconazoleresistant strain of C. albicans.
the use of the 13C-urea breath test for diagnosis of Helicobater pylori is not as sensitive as the serological tests and is not recommended for routine use.
the most important factor is the ability to identify and quantify the amount of the most important factors.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the immune system is not a static system that is either on or off.
we can’t assume that all the patients with the same diagnosis are the same.
there is no evidence of a causal relationship between the use of antibiotics and the development of type 1 diabetes.
